ownership_reason: Only the gold sees the elements together with their positions in the array and decides which occurrence of a repeated element is appended; hops 1-3 pass the list and the complete array along (an empty list is answered at hop 1), and hop 4 only calls the gold and copies the resulting list into a set, so once the gold has appended [2, 1] no caller can tell which occurrence came first. The gold's javadoc promises each element once, in the order in which the elements occur in the array, which for [1, 2, 1] is 1 then 2. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('If the list contains duplicates, these are removed (first indexed one kept)'); UniqueFilterIterator, built on UniquePredicate.evaluate ('true if this is the first time the object is seen'), returns One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six from One, Two, Three, Two, One, Four, Five, Five, Six, Five (TestUniqueFilterIterator testIterator); SetUniqueList.addAll and ListOrderedSet.addAll skip an element when an equal one is already present, so the earlier one keeps its place (TestSetUniqueList testAddAll and testIntCollectionAddAll; TestListOrderedSet testListAddReplacing). Recorded bypasses: a hop that replaces the gold call by a stable distinct of its own (LinkedHashSet), or removes the repeated elements before the gold (UniqueFilterIterator), implements the gold's decision a second time; sorting the array or reordering the refilled list passes only because the trigger input is [1, 2, 1] and breaks the documented list order.
